correctness.rationale: Exact three-digit defect algebra covers offsets 0..13 except 5,8; both remaining offsets equal -Q/2 by explicit expansion. An integral positive affine Pell recurrence preserves the conic Q=0, u odd, t divisible by 4, yielding infinitely many strictly increasing even bases with valid digit witnesses. Swart et al. (2019) Theorem 10 bounds all oasis lengths by three-digit mirage runs; an exact exhaustive integer census and positive run establish L(22)=11,L(24)=9,L(26)=11,L(28)=14. Theorem 3(2) excludes odd bases, and published Theorem 11 covers b<=20. verify.py independently checks all finite domains and recurrence identities for four iterates; the infinite part is algebraic, not inferred from tests.

value.rationale: Oasis length is the central natural invariant of the motivating 2019 paper. A Pell-induced infinite family of bases supporting fourteen consecutive parameters is a structural strengthening of the published universal five-term construction; the exact first occurrence and L(28)=14 are sharp, motivated boundary data. This is not merely a table extension, and it does not claim global unboundedness.
